Usage

Normals (N,3) -> the image2d of the Extended Gaussian Image (n_el, n_az).

A 2-D histogram of directions (Horn, *Extended Gaussian Images*, Proc. IEEE 72(12) 1984). A map of "how much surface faces which way"; for an object dominated by planes, 1 bin gets a peak. Irreversible —— it discards the directional resolution of one bin width. The discarded amount can be measured: the angle between the centre direction of the most frequent bin and the mean input direction is the quantisation error; with the default (36, 18) it is 3.7 degrees measured against a bin width of 10 degrees (reported by selftest).

The elevation bins are equal divisions of sin(el) (equal solid angle). Dividing equally in degrees makes the poles excessively fine and raises a false peak saying "faces are concentrated at the north pole".

★Passing a point cloud of positions raises no exception. backends_typed.TYPE_TO_SORT folds normals into points, so neither the evolver nor the ledger tells them apart. This op only looks at directions (it discards length), so passing (N,3) coordinates returns, plausibly, a histogram of "the direction from the origin to each point". Measured (2026-09-08, a curve of 200 points vs normals all pointing straight up): non-zero bins change 1 → 12 and the maximum bin 200 → 44, and that is all; the sum is 200 in both. "The sum matches the number of points, so it is correct" cannot tell them apart. With fullseye.set_system("extra_checks", "on"), vectors that deviate from unit length are rejected (Raises below).

Args:

normals: (N, 3).

n_az: number of azimuth bins (default 36 = 10-degree steps).

n_el: number of elevation bins (default 18).

Returns:

(n_el, n_az) float64 count map (row = elevation, column = azimuth).

Raises:

ValueError: number of bins below 1 / above the limit / invalid input.

ValueError: with extra_checks='on', when it contains vectors whose length deviates from 1 by more than 1e-6

(catches the accident of passing a point cloud of positions as normals).

The reprconv op normals_to_egi bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps n_az (default 36) and b sweeps n_el (default 18). ★The bridged op returns the fraction (the share of normals falling in each bin, summing to 1, range [0,1]) obtained by dividing the counts by the total —— to match the [0,1] contract of the declared sort image (with raw counts, values such as a maximum of 48 came out, 2026-10-07). The raw counts are returned by reprconv.normals_to_egi / fullseye.ledger.normals_to_egi.
